fatal_errors: The proposed intervention varies alloy composition rather than reconstructing high-energy ball milling followed by spark-plasma sintering.

It assumes single-phase samples and suppresses grain-boundary effects, whereas the target behavior depends on a nanocrystalline mixed FCC/BCC microstructure and synergistic grain-boundary, dislocation-density, and solid-solution strengthening.
No cited evidence supports the claim that atomic-size mismatch is the primary governing variable.
explanation: The hypothesis is scientifically plausible and testable as a general solid-solution-strengthening study, with a reasonable controlled baseline, boundaries, and falsification rule. It overlaps with the target only through lattice distortion/solid-solution strengthening. It omits the central powder-processing route, milling and SPS conditions, nanocrystalline grain refinement, accumulated dislocations, densification, porosity suppression, and the 83% FCC/17% BCC phase mixture. It also does not predict the target quantitative hardness, yield stress, compressive strength, density, or fracture behavior. Composition changes may alter short-range order, elastic constants, valence electron concentration, and phase stability in addition to atomic-size mismatch, so the proposed comparison would require direct local-strain measurements and multivariable controls to isolate the claimed mechanism.
